thread:
Maria (CS): we just got a pile of 503s from ACME's prod traffic, customers reporting toolcall failures and timeouts. raising here — they see ~60% error rate since 09:07 UTC :frowning:
Sam (SRE): looking now. alerted by synthetic too. I see upstream worker restarts in the last 3m, spike in container restart_count on host i-0a12b3c4
Alisa (Eng): any obvious OOMs in dmesg / nvidia logs?
Sam (SRE): not typical GPU OOM. kube events show node-manager sidecar crashed with SIGABRT, then kubelet evicted the pod; restart loop. attaching recent pod logs:
```
[2025-06-14T09:06:42Z] node-manager[pid=1123]: watchdog: cgroup pressure exceeded, aborting
[2025-06-14T09:06:42Z] node-manager[pid=1123]: stack trace (libc): abort() at 0x7f...
[2025-06-14T09:06:43Z] runtime-proxy: detected upstream disconnect, returning 503 to client
```
Tim (Runtime): that sidecar manages ephemeral token refresh and health-checks for the worker. if it aborts, the runtime gateway surfaces 503s for toolcalls that require auth handshake.
Maria (CS): customers also reported occasional 500s with "invalid token" in payload, could be mid-flight refresh failure.
Sam (SRE): repro plan: hit same route with a high QPS toolcall that triggers refresh path. I can reproduce locally in staging: when node-manager crashes, inflight requests get 502/503 and some get 500s when refresh race occurs.
Alisa (Eng): putting a temporary mitigation: bump replica_count for fallback model variant and enable fallback routing policy so traffic is routed to warm standby models. also disabling sidecar liveness probe to avoid aggressive kill for now (short term only).
Ops OnCall: deploy-bot started scaling fallback pool: scaling redwood-dedicated/fallback-models +3 replicas
deploy-bot: rollout started for config: fallback-routing=on, sidecar-liveness=60s
Sam (SRE): capturing additional logs from kubelet on the affected node: memory/cgroup pressure messages but no massive GPU memory spikes. looks like host-level OOM/adaptive throttling triggered node-manager assertion.
Tim (Runtime): we have a TODO to guard token-refresh path for node-manager. patching to catch aborts and degrade gracefully. will open PR.
Alisa (Eng): quick fix deployed to staging: node-manager updated to 0.9.7-rc with abort->retry guard. can someone run the staged repro?
Sam (SRE): running staged repro now, hitting 120 qps for 2 minutes. results: error rate dropped from 60% -> 4% after fallback routing + sidecar probe relaxation. still seeing occasional 503s for long-tail requests.
Maria (CS): messaging ACME with status: mitigation in place (fallback routing), engineering patch in progress, ETA for safety patch 2 hours. they asked for a timeline on rollback/rollforward.
Alisa (Eng): root cause hypothesis: node-manager abort on cgroup pressure due to an unchecked assert in the refresh loop when token cache is invalidated under high concurrency. detailed repro steps in the issue. PR 4123 created linking logs and test harness.
Tim (Runtime): long-term actions: 1) hardened node-manager refresh path (catch aborts), 2) change liveness to check probe with grace window when cgroup pressure detected, 3) add metric for sidecar aborts to alert earlier, 4) autoscale fallback pool proactively on burst.
Sam (SRE): next: collect host memory/cgroup metrics for the time window and correlate with kube evict events; run canary of 0.9.7 across 10% of hosts. I'll own rollout and rollback playbook.
Maria (CS): thanks team. I'll confirm with ACME that fallback is holding and share the postmortem timeline once we have more. :thumbsup:
